intent.raw_query: Hawaii family beach vacation, $5000, 10 days, August from Seattle

selected_hotel.name: SureStay Hotel by Best Western Buena Park Anaheim

experiences.name: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay
experiences.description: Explore one of Hawaii's most pristine marine sanctuaries with crystal-clear waters teeming with tropical fish and sea turtles. Perfect for families with kids of all ages, the bay offers calm, shallow waters ideal for beginner snorkelers. Equipment rentals are available on-site and an educational center teaches visitors about the reef ecosystem before entering the water.

experiences.name: Polynesian Cultural Center Visit
experiences.description: Spend a full day immersing the family in the rich traditions of six Polynesian cultures including Hawaiian, Samoan, Tongan, Fijian, Tahitian, and Maori. Enjoy live demonstrations, canoe rides, traditional crafts, and an incredible evening luau with fire knife dancing and an all-you-can-eat buffet. One of the most educational and entertaining family experiences on the islands.

experiences.name: Kaanapali Beach Family Day
experiences.description: Spend a leisurely day on one of America's most celebrated beaches stretching nearly three miles of golden sand on Maui's west coast. Families can swim in calm turquoise waters, build sandcastles, rent boogie boards, and watch cliff divers leap from Black Rock (Puu Kekaa) at sunset. Beachside restaurants and shave ice stands make it a perfect all-day outing.

experiences.name: Hawaii Volcanoes National Park Exploration
experiences.description: Witness the raw power of nature at one of the world's most active volcanic landscapes on the Big Island. Walk through lava tubes, hike across hardened lava fields, and peer into the glowing Kilauea caldera at dusk for a truly unforgettable family experience. The park's visitor center offers ranger-led programs designed specifically for children, making it both thrilling and educational.
experiences.location: Hawaii Volcanoes National Park, Big Island

experiences.name: Traditional Hawaiian Plate Lunch Food Tour
experiences.description: Dive into authentic Hawaiian comfort food by visiting iconic local spots serving plate lunches featuring kalua pork, lomi salmon, poi, macaroni salad, and fresh poke bowls. Stop at legendary local institutions like Helena's Hawaiian Food and grab shave ice from Matsumoto's for dessert. A delicious and affordable way to connect the whole family with Hawaii's unique culinary heritage.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Hawaii
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: SureStay Hotel by Best Western Buena Park Anaheim

experiences.name: Hawaii Volcanoes National Park Exploration
experiences.description: Witness the raw power of nature at one of the world's most active volcanic landscapes on the Big Island. Walk through lava tubes, hike across hardened lava fields, and peer into the glowing Kilauea caldera at dusk for a truly unforgettable family experience. The park's visitor center offers ranger-led programs designed specifically for children, making it both thrilling and educational.
experiences.location: Hawaii Volcanoes National Park, Big Island

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Hawaii airport at 11:20 AM — collect luggage, pick up any pre-booked rental car or take TheBus (Oahu's public transit, ~$3/ride) to your accommodation. Check in or store luggage at your hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Waikiki Beach (free entry) — relax on the sand, swim in the warm Pacific, and get your bearings. Walk the Kalakaua Avenue strip to scout affordable dining options and pick up snacks at ABC Stores.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the famous free Waikiki sunset from the beach, then stroll to Kuhio Beach Hula Show (free public hula and torch lighting ceremony at 6:30 PM nightly). Grab dinner nearby.

meals.breakfast: Grab a quick bite at the airport — Jamba Juice or a convenience snack (~$8–10)
meals.lunch: Rainbow Drive-In near Waikiki — local plate lunch (chicken or beef with rice and mac salad, ~$10–12)
meals.dinner: Marugame Udon in Waikiki — hearty udon bowls from ~$8–12, very family-friendly

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light given the 11:20 AM arrival. Use TheBus Route 20 or 42 from the airport to Waikiki (~$3 per person) to save on taxi costs. August weather averages 16–28°C with occasional rain showers — pack a light rain jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Diamond Head State Monument (parking $10/car or walk/bus free entry with $5/person hike fee). The 1.6-mile round-trip hike offers panoramic views of Honolulu and Waikiki — great for families. Start early (7–8 AM) to beat the heat and crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cool off at Hanauma Bay Nature Preserve (book online in advance, $25/adult, children under 13 free) — one of Hawaii's best snorkeling spots with colorful reef fish. Snorkel gear rental available on-site (~$12).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Waikiki area. Explore the International Market Place outdoor mall (free to browse). Enjoy a relaxed evening walk along the beachfront.

meals.breakfast: Leonard's Bakery — famous malasadas (Portuguese donuts) from $1.50 each, a Hawaii must-try
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch from Foodland supermarket near Hanauma Bay — sandwiches, fruit, and drinks (~$10–15/family)
meals.dinner: Ono Seafood — local poke bowls from ~$12–15, casual and authentic

day_by_day.notes: Hanauma Bay requires advance online reservations (book at least 2 days ahead). Bring reef-safe sunscreen — it's required by Hawaii law. TheBus Route 22 (Beach Bus) goes directly to Hanauma Bay from Waikiki (~$3).

day_by_day.morning: Explore the North Shore of Oahu — drive or take TheBus to Haleiwa Town (about 1 hour from Waikiki). Browse the charming surf town, visit local art galleries, and see the famous surf spots like Sunset Beach and Banzai Pipeline (flat in summer, safe for families).
day_by_day.afternoon: Swim and play at Waimea Bay Beach Park (free) — calm and swimmable in summer, with a famous jumping rock for older kids and teens. Picnic on the beach.
day_by_day.evening: Stop at Matsumoto Shave Ice in Haleiwa (~$4–6) — a legendary Hawaii treat. Head back to Waikiki for a quiet evening.

meals.breakfast: Kono's Northshore in Haleiwa — breakfast burritos and plates from ~$10–13
meals.lunch: Picnic at Waimea Bay — grab supplies from Foodland or Malama Market in Haleiwa (~$10–15/family)
meals.dinner: Giovanni's Shrimp Truck in Haleiwa (on the way back) — famous garlic shrimp plates ~$14–16

day_by_day.notes: North Shore is about 35 miles from Waikiki. Renting a car for this day (~$40–60/day) is most practical for families. Gas up in Honolulu as North Shore prices are higher. August is summer — North Shore waves are small and safe for swimming.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Pearl Harbor National Memorial (free entry to the grounds and museum; USS Arizona Memorial boat tour is free but requires timed-entry passes — book online in advance). A deeply moving and educational experience for the whole family.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Battleship Missouri Memorial ($32/adult, $16/child 4–12) or the Pacific Aviation Museum ($25/adult, $15/child) — both on Ford Island, accessible via shuttle from the Pearl Harbor Visitor Center.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Aloha Stadium Swap Meet (Wednesday, Saturday, Sunday — check schedule; $1 entry) for affordable local souvenirs, snacks, and people-watching. Great budget shopping for the family.

meals.breakfast: Boots & Kimo's Homestyle Kitchen in Kailua — famous macadamia nut pancakes (~$12–15), worth the short drive
meals.lunch: Pearl Harbor Visitor Center food court — sandwiches and local plates (~$10–14)
meals.dinner: Helena's Hawaiian Food (James Beard Award winner) — authentic Hawaiian plates like kalua pig and lomi salmon (~$12–18)

day_by_day.notes: Pearl Harbor is free but very popular — arrive early or book timed passes online weeks in advance. The USS Arizona Memorial may have limited availability. Allow at least 3–4 hours for the full Pearl Harbor experience.

day_by_day.morning: Take an inter-island flight to the Big Island (Hawaii Island) — budget airlines like Southwest or Hawaiian Airlines offer inter-island flights from ~$59–99 one way. Fly into Kona or Hilo airport. This is the day to travel to the Big Island for the volcano experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Hawaii Volcanoes National Park (entry $35/car, valid 7 days — great value for families). Stop at the Kilauea Visitor Center to get oriented, then walk the Crater Rim Trail to see the Halema'uma'u Crater and active lava lake views.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the glowing lava lake after dark from the Kilauea Overlook — one of Hawaii's most spectacular free natural shows. The glow intensifies after sunset.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast at Honolulu airport before your flight — Starbucks or local café (~$8–12)
meals.lunch: Cafe Ono inside the Volcano Art Center near the park — sandwiches and local fare (~$10–14)
meals.dinner: Thai Thai Restaurant in Volcano Village (just outside the park) — affordable Thai-Hawaiian fusion from ~$12–16

day_by_day.notes: Book inter-island flights well in advance for best budget prices. Rent a car on the Big Island (~$40–60/day) — public transit is very limited. Bring layers as Volcano area elevation (~4,000 ft) makes it cooler and rainier than the coast. Check NPS website for current lava activity status.

day_by_day.morning: Return to Hawaii Volcanoes National Park for morning exploration — hike the Devastation Trail (easy, 1 mile) and the Thurston Lava Tube (free with park entry, a magical underground tunnel through hardened lava). Perfect for kids.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive the Chain of Craters Road (free with park entry) — a stunning 19-mile scenic drive descending 3,700 feet to the coast, passing ancient lava flows, pit craters, and petroglyphs. Stop at the Holei Sea Arch at the road's end.
day_by_day.evening: Drive to Hilo town (~45 min from the park). Stroll the charming downtown, visit the Hilo Farmers Market area, and enjoy a relaxed evening by Hilo Bay.

meals.breakfast: Volcano House Restaurant inside the park — buffet breakfast with crater views (~$18/adult, ~$10/child, splurge-worthy for the view)
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic — grab supplies from KTA Super Stores in Hilo the night before (~$10–15/family)
meals.dinner: Puka Puka Kitchen in Hilo — local Hawaiian comfort food, plates from ~$10–14

day_by_day.notes: The Chain of Craters Road is one of the most dramatic drives in the US — don't miss it. Wear sturdy closed-toe shoes for lava field walking. The Thurston Lava Tube can be crowded midday — visit early morning for a quieter experience.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Rainbow Falls in Hilo (free) — a beautiful 80-foot waterfall best seen in morning light when rainbows form in the mist. Then explore Akaka Falls State Park (~$5/car) — a stunning 442-foot waterfall accessible via an easy 0.4-mile loop trail through lush rainforest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Kohala Coast — drive to Hapuna Beach State Recreation Area (free, small parking fee ~$10) — consistently rated one of Hawaii's best beaches with calm, clear water perfect for families. Swim and snorkel.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the historic Kawaihae Harbor area. Drive through Waimea (Kamuela) town for a taste of upcountry Hawaii — cowboy culture meets Hawaiian tradition.

meals.breakfast: Cafe 100 in Hilo — famous for the original Loco Moco (rice, hamburger patty, egg, gravy) from ~$6–9
meals.lunch: Picnic at Hapuna Beach — pack supplies from Island Naturals Market in Hilo (~$10–15/family)
meals.dinner: Village Burger in Waimea — Big Island grass-fed beef burgers from ~$12–15, family-friendly

day_by_day.notes: Akaka Falls is about 15 miles north of Hilo — combine with Rainbow Falls for an efficient morning. Hapuna Beach is about 1 hour from Hilo on the west coast. August is peak summer — Hapuna can get busy on weekends, arrive by 10 AM for good parking.

day_by_day.morning: Take an inter-island flight to Maui (Hawaiian Airlines or Southwest, ~$59–99 one way). Fly into Kahului Airport. Pick up rental car and head to the Road to Hana — start the famous scenic drive early. Stop at Twin Falls (free, easy hike) and Waikamoi Nature Trail.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Road to Hana — stop at Ke'anae Peninsula (free, stunning coastal views), Wailua Valley State Wayside (free overlook), and the black sand beach at Wai'anapanapa State Park ($5/person entry, book online in advance — required).
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Hana town. Explore the small, charming town. Watch the sunset from Hana Bay Beach Park (free).

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast at Kahului Airport or a local café before starting the drive (~$8–12)
meals.lunch: Halfway to Hana food stand — banana bread (~$5–7) and fresh fruit smoothies, a Road to Hana tradition
meals.dinner: Hana Ranch Restaurant — local plates and burgers from ~$14–18, one of few options in Hana

day_by_day.notes: The Road to Hana is 64 miles but takes 3–4 hours one way due to 620 curves and 59 bridges. Start by 8 AM to avoid traffic. Wai'anapanapa State Park requires advance online reservations — book weeks ahead. Gas up in Kahului before starting — there are no gas stations along the route.

day_by_day.morning: Drive back from Hana via the southern route (past Oheo Gulch/Seven Sacred Pools in Haleakala National Park — $35/car entry, valid 3 days). Hike the Pipiwai Trail (4 miles round trip) through bamboo forest to the stunning 400-foot Waimoku Falls — one of Maui's best hikes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Kaanapali Beach on Maui's west coast (about 2 hours from Hana) — a beautiful family beach with calm water. Snorkel at Black Rock (Pu'u Keka'a) — free snorkeling with sea turtles and colorful fish.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll the Kaanapali Beachfront Walk (free). Watch the free cliff diving ceremony at Black Rock at sunset — a Maui tradition performed nightly at the Sheraton. Browse the Whalers Village outdoor mall.

meals.breakfast: Brunch at Hana Farms (near Hana) — fresh local food from ~$10–14 before departing
meals.lunch: Ululani's Hawaiian Shave Ice in Lahaina — shave ice from ~$5–8 plus grab a quick bite at Lahaina's food trucks (~$10–12)
meals.dinner: Aloha Mixed Plate in Kaanapali — oceanfront local Hawaiian food, plates from ~$13–17, great family atmosphere

day_by_day.notes: The Oheo Gulch swimming pools may be closed due to flash flood risk — check NPS website before visiting. The southern return route from Hana adds about 30 minutes but offers different scenery. Kaanapali is about 4 miles north of Lahaina — easy to combine both in the afternoon.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning on Maui — visit the Maui Ocean Center in Maalaea ($30/adult, $20/child 3–12) — Hawaii's premier aquarium with sharks, rays, and Hawaiian green sea turtles. Excellent for families and educational for kids.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Kanaha Beach Park in Kahului (free) — a local favorite beach near the airport, perfect for a final swim and relaxation before departure. Pack up, return rental car, and head to Kahului Airport for your return flight.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Maui — fly back to the mainland. Reflect on 10 incredible days of Hawaiian adventure!

meals.breakfast: Kihei Caffe in Kihei — hearty local breakfast plates from ~$10–14, a Maui institution
meals.lunch: Tin Roof Maui in Kahului (Chef Sheldon Simeon's casual spot) — local plates from ~$12–16, near the airport
meals.dinner: Airport dining or in-flight — grab snacks at Kahului Airport for the flight home (~$10–15)

day_by_day.notes: Maui Ocean Center opens at 9 AM — arrive early to beat crowds and have time for the beach afterward. Return rental car at least 2 hours before your flight. Check airline baggage policies if you've purchased local goods or souvenirs. Total estimated budget for 10 days (per adult): flights ~$300–500, accommodation ~$600–900, food ~$300–400, activities ~$200–300, transport ~$200–300 — approximately $1,600–2,400 per adult for a budget-conscious trip.

trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Flight arrives at 11:20 AM — no morning activities scheduled. Upon landing, collect luggage, pick up rental car or arrange shuttle transfer to accommodation area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to SureStay Hotel by Best Western Buena Park. Note: The hotel is located in Buena Park, California — use this afternoon to rest, freshen up, and prepare for the Hawaii trip. Visit a nearby grocery store or pharmacy to stock up on travel essentials, sunscreen, and snacks for the journey.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Buena Park/Anaheim area for a relaxed first evening. Stroll through a nearby shopping center or take a short drive to scope out the neighborhood. Early bedtime recommended to recover from travel.

meals.breakfast: Grab a bite at the airport before or after landing — try a café or quick-service restaurant inside the terminal.
meals.lunch: In-N-Out Burger (nearby Buena Park location) — a classic California mid-range option, around $10–15 per person.
meals.dinner: Lucille's Smokehouse Bar-B-Que on Beach Blvd, Buena Park — hearty American BBQ, mid-range pricing around $20–30 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is a travel and recovery day based in Buena Park, CA. Confirm Hawaii inter-island flight or main Hawaii flight details for Day 2. Lay out all gear and confirm snorkeling equipment, reef-safe sunscreen, and family documents are packed.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning departure from Buena Park hotel. Head to LAX or John Wayne Airport (SNA) for your flight to Honolulu, Oahu (approximately 5–6 hour flight). Arrive in Honolulu mid-morning to early afternoon depending on departure time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to your Honolulu accommodation (Waikiki area recommended for families). Once settled, take a gentle introductory walk along Waikiki Beach — let the kids dip their toes in the warm Pacific Ocean. The beach is calm and family-friendly, perfect for a low-key first Hawaii afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along Kalakaua Avenue, Waikiki's main boulevard. Watch the free hula and live music performances that take place nightly at Kuhio Beach Hula Mound (free, starts around 6:30 PM). A wonderful, authentic welcome to Hawaii.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or airport café before departure — budget $10–15 per person.
meals.lunch: Rainbow Drive-In, Honolulu — a legendary local plate lunch spot, very affordable at $10–14 per person. Great introduction to Hawaiian comfort food.
meals.dinner: Duke's Waikiki at the Outrigger Waikiki — iconic beachfront restaurant with Hawaiian-inspired dishes, mid-range at $25–40 per person. Reservations recommended.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm Hawaii accommodation check-in time in advance. Pick up a rental car at Honolulu airport if planning to explore beyond Waikiki. August weather in Hawaii averages around 85°F (29°C) with occasional brief showers — pack a light rain jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay — one of Hawaii's most pristine marine sanctuaries. Arrive early (gates open at 6:45 AM) as entry is limited and reservations are required in advance. Explore crystal-clear waters teeming with tropical fish, sea turtles, and vibrant coral. A mandatory 9-minute educational video is shown before entry. Perfect for families with children.
day_by_day.afternoon: After Hanauma Bay, drive the scenic Makapu'u Point Lighthouse Trail (2.5-mile round trip, paved, family-friendly) for stunning panoramic views of the southeastern Oahu coastline. In August, you may spot humpback whales in the distance. Finish with a stop at Makapu'u Beach for photos.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Waikiki. Relax at the hotel pool or beach before dinner. Browse the International Market Place open-air shopping center for souvenirs and gifts.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel or grab malasadas (Portuguese donuts) from Leonard's Bakery — a Hawaii institution, under $10.
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch from a nearby Foodland or Times Supermarket to enjoy at Hanauma Bay's picnic area — budget-friendly at $8–12 per person.
meals.dinner: Ono Seafood, Honolulu — a beloved local poke shop with fresh ahi poke bowls, around $15–20 per person. Casual and delicious.

day_by_day.notes: Hanauma Bay reservations MUST be made online in advance at hawaiistateparks.org. Entry fee is $25 per adult, children 12 and under are free. Apply reef-safe sunscreen only — chemical sunscreens are banned at the bay. Bring water shoes for the rocky entry.

day_by_day.morning: Polynesian Cultural Center Visit — spend a full day immersing the family in the rich traditions of six Polynesian cultures (Hawaiian, Samoan, Tongan, Fijian, Tahitian, and Māori). The center opens at 11:45 AM, so enjoy a leisurely morning before heading to Laie on the North Shore (about 1 hour drive from Waikiki). Explore the village exhibits and interactive cultural demonstrations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the Polynesian Cultural Center's six island villages. Participate in hands-on activities like coconut husking, spear throwing, and traditional weaving. Watch the spectacular canoe pageant on the lagoon (typically at 2:30 PM) — a highlight for families with colorful performances from each culture.
day_by_day.evening: Stay for the world-famous 'Ha: Breath of Life' evening show (included with most packages) — a breathtaking theatrical production featuring fire dancing, acrobatics, and traditional music. Dinner at the center's Ali'i Luau (book in advance) for an authentic Hawaiian feast.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a smoothie bowl from Açaí Bowls Hawaii in Waikiki — around $12–15.
meals.lunch: Gateway Bar & Grill inside the Polynesian Cultural Center — included with many admission packages, or available à la carte for $15–20.
meals.dinner: Ali'i Luau at the Polynesian Cultural Center — all-inclusive luau dinner with traditional Hawaiian food (kalua pig, poi, haupia). Approximately $120–140 per adult, $75–90 per child. Book well in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Purchase Polynesian Cultural Center tickets online in advance at polynesia.com — combo packages including the luau and evening show offer the best value. The center is located in Laie, about 38 miles from Waikiki. Plan for a full day (11 AM–9:30 PM). Closed on Sundays.

day_by_day.morning: Traditional Hawaiian Plate Lunch Food Tour — dive into authentic Hawaiian comfort food by visiting iconic local spots across Honolulu. Start at Helena's Hawaiian Food (a James Beard Award winner) for pipikaula short ribs and lomi salmon. Then visit Zippy's for saimin noodle soup, a Hawaii staple.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Chinatown Honolulu — a vibrant historic district with colorful markets, art galleries, and local eateries. Visit the Oahu Market for fresh tropical fruits and local snacks. Walk to the nearby Iolani Palace, the only royal palace on U.S. soil, for a guided family tour (approximately 1 hour, $22 adults, $6 children).
day_by_day.evening: Head to Ala Moana Beach Park for a relaxed sunset swim and beach time. The park is large, calm, and very family-friendly with a protected reef creating gentle swimming conditions. Watch the sunset over the Waianae Mountains.

meals.breakfast: Helena's Hawaiian Food — try the traditional Hawaiian breakfast plate with laulau and rice, around $15–18.
meals.lunch: Zippy's Restaurant — Hawaii's beloved local chain serving saimin, chili rice, and plate lunches. Budget-friendly at $10–15 per person.
meals.dinner: Mariposa at Neiman Marcus, Ala Moana Center — elegant but accessible, known for their famous popovers and fresh island cuisine. Mid-range at $30–45 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Helena's Hawaiian Food is closed on Sundays and Mondays — confirm hours before visiting. The food tour is self-guided and flexible. Iolani Palace tours should be booked online in advance at iolanipalace.org. Bring cash for Chinatown market vendors.

day_by_day.morning: Fly from Honolulu (HNL) to Kahului, Maui (OGG) — a short 35-minute inter-island flight. Book with Hawaiian Airlines or Southwest. Arrive in Maui, pick up rental car, and check in to your Maui accommodation (Kaanapali or Lahaina area recommended). Drive the scenic road toward West Maui.
day_by_day.afternoon: Kaanapali Beach Family Day — spend a leisurely afternoon on one of America's most celebrated beaches, stretching nearly three miles of golden sand. Swim in the warm, calm waters, build sandcastles, and snorkel around Black Rock (Pu'u Keka'a) at the north end of the beach where sea turtles and tropical fish are commonly spotted.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the legendary Cliff Diving Ceremony at Black Rock — every evening at sunset, a torch lighter performs a traditional Hawaiian ceremony followed by a cliff dive into the ocean. It's free to watch from the beach and is a magical family experience.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast at the Kahului Airport café or a local spot near your accommodation after check-in.
meals.lunch: Hula Grill Kaanapali — beachfront restaurant with fresh fish tacos, burgers, and Hawaiian-inspired dishes. Mid-range at $20–30 per person. Eat with your toes in the sand.
meals.dinner: Leilani's on the Beach, Kaanapali — casual oceanfront dining with fresh seafood and Hawaiian classics. Mid-range at $25–40 per person. Watch the sunset over Lanai and Molokai.

day_by_day.notes: Book inter-island flights at least 2–3 weeks in advance for best prices (typically $60–120 per person each way). Kaanapali Beach has free public beach access with paid parking lots nearby. Black Rock snorkeling is best in the morning but afternoon is still excellent. Bring reef-safe sunscreen.

day_by_day.morning: Road to Hana — embark on one of the world's most scenic drives along Maui's northeastern coastline. Start early (7 AM) to beat traffic. Stop at Twin Falls for a short family-friendly hike to beautiful waterfalls (30 minutes round trip). Continue to Wai'anapanapa State Park to see the stunning black sand beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Road to Hana, stopping at Hana Town for lunch. Visit the Pools of 'Ohe'o (Seven Sacred Pools) in Haleakalā National Park — a series of cascading freshwater pools perfect for swimming (when open). The short Pipiwai Trail leads to a stunning bamboo forest and 400-foot Waimoku Falls.
day_by_day.evening: Begin the return drive back to Kaanapali (approximately 2.5–3 hours). Alternatively, stay overnight in Hana for a more relaxed experience. Arrive back at the hotel for a well-deserved rest.

meals.breakfast: Pack a picnic breakfast from a Maui grocery store (Safeway or Foodland) the night before — enjoy at Twin Falls, around $8–12 per person.
meals.lunch: Hana Farms Kitchen in Hana Town — fresh local food including banana bread, smoothies, and plate lunches. Budget-friendly at $12–18 per person.
meals.dinner: Aloha Mixed Plate, Lahaina — casual beachfront restaurant with generous Hawaiian plate lunches and local favorites. Mid-range at $18–25 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Road to Hana has 620 curves and 59 bridges — not recommended for those prone to motion sickness. Download an offline map or use the Shaka Guide Road to Hana audio tour app ($10) for narrated stops. Wai'anapanapa State Park requires advance reservations at hawaiistateparks.org ($5 per person). Start early to avoid crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Haleakalā Sunrise Experience — wake up at 2:30 AM to drive to the summit of Haleakalā volcano (10,023 feet) to witness one of the world's most spectacular sunrises above the clouds. The experience is otherworldly and deeply moving. Dress in warm layers — summit temperatures can drop to 40°F (4°C) even in August.
day_by_day.afternoon: After descending from Haleakalā, stop at Kula for breakfast at a local farm café. Visit the Ali'i Kula Lavender Farm for a family-friendly stroll through fragrant lavender fields with panoramic Maui views. Then head to Makena Beach (Big Beach) — one of Maui's most beautiful and expansive beaches for an afternoon swim.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Kaanapali for a relaxing evening. Enjoy a sunset stroll along the Kaanapali Boardwalk. Treat the family to shave ice at Ululani's Hawaiian Shave Ice — a Maui institution.

meals.breakfast: Sunrise snacks packed from the hotel (granola bars, fruit, hot coffee in a thermos) for the summit. After descending, stop at Kula Bistro for a full farm-fresh breakfast — mid-range at $15–20 per person.
meals.lunch: Café O'Lei at the Dunes, Maui — fresh salads, sandwiches, and local specials. Mid-range at $18–25 per person.
meals.dinner: Monkeypod Kitchen by Merriman, Kaanapali — farm-to-table Hawaiian cuisine with craft cocktails and live music nightly. Mid-range at $30–45 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Haleakalā National Park sunrise reservations are MANDATORY and must be booked at recreation.gov up to 60 days in advance ($1 reservation fee plus $30 park entrance fee per vehicle). Spots sell out within minutes of opening. Bring warm layers, gloves, and a blanket. The drive from Kaanapali to the summit takes approximately 1.5–2 hours.

day_by_day.morning: Fly from Kahului, Maui (OGG) to Kona or Hilo, Big Island (KOA or ITO) — approximately 45-minute inter-island flight. Check in to Big Island accommodation near Volcano Village or Hilo. Head directly to Hawaii Volcanoes National Park — one of the world's most active volcanic landscapes. Begin at the Kilauea Visitor Center for orientation and ranger talks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Hawaii Volcanoes National Park — drive the 11-mile Crater Rim Drive for dramatic views of Kilauea Caldera. Walk the Devastation Trail (0.6 miles, easy, family-friendly) through a surreal landscape of hardened lava and recovering vegetation. Visit the Thurston Lava Tube (Nāhuku) — a 500-year-old lava tube that kids absolutely love.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Kilauea Caldera overlook at dusk — if there is active lava glow, the caldera illuminates in an eerie red-orange light that is absolutely unforgettable. Check with park rangers for current volcanic activity updates.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a quick stop at a Hilo café such as Café 100 — famous for their loco moco (rice, hamburger patty, egg, and gravy), around $10–14.
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch to enjoy at one of the park's scenic overlooks — purchase supplies from KTA Super Stores in Hilo, around $10–15 per person.
meals.dinner: Kilauea Lodge Restaurant, Volcano Village — cozy, romantic lodge restaurant with European-Hawaiian fusion cuisine. Mid-range at $30–45 per person. Warm and welcoming after a day of exploration.

day_by_day.notes: Hawaii Volcanoes National Park entrance fee is $30 per vehicle (valid for 7 days). The park is open 24 hours. Volcanic activity is dynamic — check nps.gov/havo for current eruption status before visiting. Wear closed-toe shoes and bring a light jacket as elevation makes it cooler. Volcanic fumes (vog) can be irritating — those with respiratory conditions should take precautions.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning on the Big Island — visit Rainbow Falls (Waiānuenue) in Hilo, a stunning 80-foot waterfall that creates rainbows in the morning mist (best viewed 9–10 AM). A short, easy walk from the parking area — perfect for families. Then explore Hilo Farmers Market (open Tuesday and Saturday) for fresh tropical fruits, local crafts, and Hawaiian honey.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Hapuna Beach State Recreation Area on the Kohala Coast — consistently ranked one of the best beaches in the United States. Enjoy a final afternoon of swimming, snorkeling, and relaxing on the white sand beach. The calm, clear waters are ideal for families. Depart for the airport (Kona KOA or Hilo ITO) for your return flight.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Big Island for return flight to the mainland. Reflect on an incredible 10-day Hawaii adventure filled with beaches, culture, volcanoes, and family memories. Safe travels!

meals.breakfast: Café Pesto, Hilo — fresh pastries, eggs, and local coffee with a beautiful bay view. Mid-range at $14–18 per person.
meals.lunch: Hapuna Beach Grille at the beach park — casual beachside food with burgers, sandwiches, and shave ice. Budget-friendly at $12–18 per person.
meals.dinner: Airport dining at Kona International Airport or grab a final plate lunch from Island Lava Java near the airport — around $15–20 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm return flight details and arrive at the airport at least 2 hours before departure. Hilo Farmers Market is most vibrant on Wednesday and Saturday — Tuesday is smaller but still worthwhile. Purchase final souvenirs at the farmers market for the best prices and most authentic local products. Macadamia nuts, Kona coffee, and Hawaiian sea salt make excellent gifts.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Hawaii Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: SureStay Hotel by Best Western Buena Park Anaheim

experiences.name: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay
experiences.description: Explore one of Hawaii's most pristine marine sanctuaries with crystal-clear waters teeming with tropical fish and sea turtles. Perfect for families with kids of all ages, the bay offers calm, shallow waters ideal for beginner snorkelers. Equipment rentals are available on-site and an educational center teaches visitors about the reef ecosystem before entering the water.

experiences.name: Polynesian Cultural Center Visit
experiences.description: Spend a full day immersing the family in the rich traditions of six Polynesian cultures including Hawaiian, Samoan, Tongan, Fijian, Tahitian, and Maori. Enjoy live demonstrations, canoe rides, traditional crafts, and an incredible evening luau with fire knife dancing and an all-you-can-eat buffet. One of the most educational and entertaining family experiences on the islands.

experiences.name: Kaanapali Beach Family Day
experiences.description: Spend a leisurely day on one of America's most celebrated beaches stretching nearly three miles of golden sand on Maui's west coast. Families can swim in calm turquoise waters, build sandcastles, rent boogie boards, and watch cliff divers leap from Black Rock (Puu Kekaa) at sunset. Beachside restaurants and shave ice stands make it a perfect all-day outing.

experiences.name: Hawaii Volcanoes National Park Exploration
experiences.description: Witness the raw power of nature at one of the world's most active volcanic landscapes on the Big Island. Walk through lava tubes, hike across hardened lava fields, and peer into the glowing Kilauea caldera at dusk for a truly unforgettable family experience. The park's visitor center offers ranger-led programs designed specifically for children, making it both thrilling and educational.
experiences.location: Hawaii Volcanoes National Park, Big Island

experiences.name: Traditional Hawaiian Plate Lunch Food Tour
experiences.description: Dive into authentic Hawaiian comfort food by visiting iconic local spots serving plate lunches featuring kalua pork, lomi salmon, poi, macaroni salad, and fresh poke bowls. Stop at legendary local institutions like Helena's Hawaiian Food and grab shave ice from Matsumoto's for dessert. A delicious and affordable way to connect the whole family with Hawaii's unique culinary heritage.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at 11:20 — Flight Alaska lands. Clear customs, collect luggage, and arrange private luxury transfer to hotel. Check in early if possible at SureStay Hotel by Best Western Buena Park Anaheim and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Settle into the hotel and take a leisurely stroll around the Buena Park area. Visit a nearby shopping center or relax at the hotel pool to recover from travel. Pick up any last-minute Hawaii essentials at a local pharmacy or store.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a welcome dinner at a nearby upscale restaurant to celebrate the start of the trip. Explore the Buena Park dining scene and retire early to prepare for the Hawaii-bound flight the next morning.

meals.breakfast: Light snack or meal on the Alaska Airlines flight before landing
meals.lunch: The Catch Restaurant & Bar in Buena Park — casual upscale seafood to ease into the vacation mood
meals.dinner: Knotts Berry Farm area fine dining or Anaheim White House Restaurant — elegant Italian-American cuisine in a historic setting

day_by_day.notes: Nothing is scheduled before 11:20 AM arrival. Focus Day 1 on rest and recovery. Confirm Hawaii hotel reservations and pre-book all experiences in advance. Pack reef-safe sunscreen for Hanauma Bay visit later in the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Buena Park early for LAX or John Wayne Airport for the inter-island flight to Honolulu, Oahu. Arrive in Honolulu and check in to a luxury oceanfront resort such as the Halekulani Hotel or The Royal Hawaiian on Waikiki Beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: After check-in, head straight to Waikiki Beach for a relaxed first afternoon in Hawaii. Rent premium beach chairs and umbrellas, take a gentle swim in the warm Pacific, and let the family soak in the iconic views of Diamond Head.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the hotel's oceanfront bar followed by a premium welcome dinner featuring fresh Hawaiian seafood and local flavors.

meals.breakfast: Airport lounge breakfast or grab-and-go from a premium café before departure
meals.lunch: Duke's Waikiki — iconic beachfront restaurant with fresh fish tacos, poke bowls, and tropical cocktails
meals.dinner: La Mer at Halekulani — Hawaii's most celebrated fine dining restaurant offering French-inspired cuisine with Pacific ingredients and stunning ocean views

day_by_day.notes: Book the luxury resort well in advance. Request an ocean-view room or suite for the full Hawaii experience. The Royal Hawaiian (The Pink Palace) is especially family-friendly with premium amenities. Weather in August averages 16.8°C highs with some rain — pack a light rain jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning visit to Hanauma Bay Nature Preserve for world-class snorkeling. Arrive before 8:00 AM to beat crowds and secure the best spots. The bay is a protected marine sanctuary teeming with sea turtles, tropical fish, and vibrant coral. Snorkel gear rental available on-site or bring premium gear from the resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Waikiki for lunch, then take a private guided Diamond Head Crater hike for panoramic views of Oahu's coastline. The moderate 1.6-mile round-trip trail is suitable for families and rewards hikers with breathtaking summit views.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a traditional Hawaiian sunset luau experience at a premium venue such as the Royal Hawaiian Luau on the beach — complete with fire dancers, live music, and a lavish buffet of Hawaiian specialties.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the hotel before heading to Hanauma Bay — açaí bowls, fresh tropical fruit, and Kona coffee
meals.lunch: Orchids at Halekulani — elegant oceanfront dining with fresh catch of the day and Hawaiian-inspired salads
meals.dinner: Royal Hawaiian Luau — all-inclusive premium luau dinner featuring kalua pig, poi, lomi salmon, haupia, and tropical cocktails on the beach

day_by_day.notes: Hanauma Bay requires advance reservations online — book at least 2 weeks ahead as spots fill quickly. The bay is closed on Tuesdays. Apply reef-safe sunscreen only. Children must be supervised in the water at all times. The luau typically runs 2–3 hours starting at sunset around 6:00 PM.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day immersive experience at the Polynesian Cultural Center on Oahu's North Shore. Spend the morning exploring six authentic Polynesian village recreations — Hawaii, Samoa, Tonga, Fiji, Tahiti, and Aotearoa. Participate in hands-on cultural activities including coconut husking, fire-making, and traditional weaving.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the Polynesian Cultural Center with the IMAX film 'Hā: Breath of Life' and the canoe pageant on the lagoon. Browse the premium gift shops for authentic Polynesian crafts and souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Attend the spectacular 'Hā: Breath of Life' evening show — a world-class theatrical production featuring over 100 performers, fire knife dancing, and stunning choreography. Enjoy the Ambassador Dinner Package for premium seating and a gourmet buffet.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast buffet featuring fresh Hawaiian fruits, macadamia nut pancakes, and Kona coffee
meals.lunch: Gateway Buffet at the Polynesian Cultural Center — extensive spread of Hawaiian and Polynesian dishes including poi, laulau, and fresh pineapple
meals.dinner: Ambassador Luau Dinner at the Polynesian Cultural Center — premium reserved seating with a gourmet buffet and priority access to the evening show

day_by_day.notes: The Polynesian Cultural Center is approximately 35 miles from Waikiki — arrange a private luxury van transfer for the family. The full-day experience runs from approximately 11:30 AM to 9:30 PM. Book the Ambassador Package well in advance for the best experience. Note that Hanauma Bay is closed today (Tuesday) — perfect day for this alternative.

day_by_day.morning: Take a private luxury catamaran sailing tour along Oahu's coastline. Depart from Honolulu Harbor for a morning of snorkeling, dolphin watching, and sailing with a professional crew. Premium tours include snorkel gear, paddleboards, and gourmet snacks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the historic Pearl Harbor National Memorial for a moving and educational family experience. Tour the USS Arizona Memorial, USS Missouri Battleship, and the Pacific Aviation Museum. Book a premium guided tour for priority access and expert narration.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Waikiki for a relaxed evening. Stroll the Kalakaua Avenue luxury shopping strip — Chanel, Louis Vuitton, Tiffany & Co. — before a refined dinner at one of Honolulu's top restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Eggs 'n Things Waikiki — beloved local institution famous for macadamia nut pancakes and fresh tropical fruit crepes
meals.lunch: Gourmet snacks and tropical beverages provided on the private catamaran sailing tour
meals.dinner: Nobu Honolulu — world-renowned Japanese-Peruvian fusion restaurant with premium omakase options and fresh Hawaiian seafood

day_by_day.notes: Pearl Harbor requires advance timed-entry reservations — book online at recreation.gov. The USS Arizona Memorial boat tour is free but timed tickets are essential. Children under 4 are not permitted on the USS Arizona boat. The catamaran tour should be booked through the hotel concierge for a premium private experience.

day_by_day.morning: Fly inter-island from Honolulu to Maui (approximately 30-minute flight). Check in to a luxury resort on Kaanapali Beach such as the Hyatt Regency Maui or the Westin Maui Resort & Spa. Both offer premium family amenities including multiple pools, waterslides, and direct beach access.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at Kaanapali Beach — one of America's most celebrated beaches stretching nearly three miles of golden sand. Rent premium beach equipment, try stand-up paddleboarding, or take a family surf lesson with a certified instructor. The calm, clear waters are ideal for all ages.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the legendary Cliff Diver ceremony at Black Rock (Pu'u Keka'a) at sunset — a nightly tradition where a torch-lit diver leaps from the lava rock into the ocean. Follow with a premium beachfront dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before the inter-island flight — fresh papaya, granola, and Kona coffee
meals.lunch: Leilani's on the Beach at Whalers Village — upscale open-air beachfront dining with fresh fish, lobster, and tropical cocktails directly on Kaanapali Beach
meals.dinner: Japengo at Hyatt Regency Maui — award-winning Pacific Rim cuisine with sushi, fresh Hawaiian fish, and panoramic ocean views

day_by_day.notes: Book the inter-island flight on Hawaiian Airlines for the most reliable service. Arrange a private luxury transfer from Kahului Airport to Kaanapali (approximately 45 minutes). Kaanapali Beach is consistently rated one of the top beaches in the USA — the water is calm and family-friendly. The Cliff Diver ceremony occurs nightly at sunset, typically around 6:00 PM.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn departure for the legendary Haleakala Sunrise experience. A private luxury van will transport the family to the summit of Haleakala volcano (10,023 feet) to witness one of the world's most spectacular sunrises above the clouds. Bring warm layers as summit temperatures can drop to near freezing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend from Haleakala and visit the charming upcountry Maui town of Makawao for artisan shopping and local culture. Then head to the Road to Hana for a scenic drive stopping at Twin Falls, Garden of Eden Arboretum, and Wailua Falls — one of Hawaii's most photogenic waterfalls.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Kaanapali for a relaxing evening at the resort. Enjoy the hotel's premium spa facilities — couples massage, hot tubs, and oceanfront relaxation.

meals.breakfast: Sunrise snack pack prepared by the hotel — thermoses of Kona coffee, pastries, and fresh fruit to enjoy at the Haleakala summit
meals.lunch: Mama's Fish House in Paia — one of Hawaii's most iconic and acclaimed restaurants featuring ultra-fresh fish caught by local fishermen, named on the menu daily
meals.dinner: Merriman's Maui in Kapalua — farm-to-table Hawaiian Regional Cuisine pioneer with stunning sunset ocean views and locally sourced ingredients

day_by_day.notes: Haleakala National Park requires advance timed sunrise reservations — book at recreation.gov up to 60 days in advance as these sell out immediately. Dress in warm layers (temperatures at the summit can be 15–20°C colder than the beach). Mama's Fish House requires reservations weeks in advance — book immediately. The Road to Hana is a full experience — consider doing just the highlights if traveling with young children.

day_by_day.morning: Morning snorkeling tour at Molokini Crater — a partially submerged volcanic crater off Maui's coast offering some of Hawaii's clearest water (visibility up to 150 feet) and abundant marine life. Book a premium private charter for the family with a professional marine naturalist guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Maui Ocean Center — the Western Hemisphere's largest tropical aquarium. Explore exhibits featuring Hawaiian green sea turtles, hammerhead sharks, manta rays, and a stunning walk-through underwater tunnel. Excellent for families with children of all ages.
day_by_day.evening: Traditional Hawaiian Plate Lunch Food Tour in Lahaina town — visit iconic local spots serving plate lunches featuring kalua pork, loco moco, garlic shrimp, and fresh poke. A premium guided food tour provides insider access to the best local establishments.

meals.breakfast: Early continental breakfast at the resort before the Molokini boat departure
meals.lunch: Gourmet deli lunch provided on the private Molokini charter — fresh sandwiches, tropical fruit, and beverages
meals.dinner: Lahaina Grill — one of Maui's most celebrated fine dining restaurants featuring contemporary American cuisine with Hawaiian influences in a historic Lahaina setting

day_by_day.notes: Molokini Crater charters depart early (typically 6:30–7:00 AM) to arrive before afternoon winds pick up. Book a premium private charter through the hotel concierge for the best experience. The Maui Ocean Center is excellent for families and typically takes 2–3 hours. Note that historic Lahaina was severely impacted by the 2023 wildfires — check current conditions and support local businesses during your visit.

day_by_day.morning: Fly inter-island from Maui to the Big Island (Hawaii Island). Check in to a luxury resort on the Kohala Coast such as the Four Seasons Resort Hualalai or the Mauna Kea Beach Hotel. Both offer world-class amenities, private beaches, and exceptional family programs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Hawaii Volcanoes National Park — approximately 1.5 hours from the Kohala Coast. Witness the raw power of Kilauea, one of the world's most active volcanoes. Walk the Kilauea Iki Trail through a hardened lava lake, explore lava tubes at Thurston Lava Tube, and view the glowing Halemaumau Crater.
day_by_day.evening: If lava is actively flowing (check NPS website for current conditions), arrange a premium guided evening lava viewing tour for a once-in-a-lifetime experience of molten lava meeting the ocean. Return to the resort for a late dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast at the Maui resort before the inter-island flight
meals.lunch: Cafe Ohia at the Volcano House Hotel inside Hawaii Volcanoes National Park — the only restaurant inside the park with views of the Kilauea Caldera
meals.dinner: ULU Ocean Grill at Four Seasons Hualalai — award-winning oceanfront restaurant featuring locally sourced Hawaiian ingredients with stunning Pacific views

day_by_day.notes: Hawaii Volcanoes National Park is open 24 hours and the $35 per vehicle entrance fee is valid for 7 days. Volcanic activity changes daily — check the USGS Hawaiian Volcano Observatory website for current eruption status. Wear closed-toe shoes and bring a light jacket as the park sits at 4,000 feet elevation. Volcanic fumes (vog) can be irritating — those with respiratory conditions should take precautions.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning on the Big Island — enjoy a premium manta ray night snorkel or early morning whale watching tour (seasonal) from the Kohala Coast. Alternatively, visit the stunning Hapuna Beach State Recreation Area — consistently rated one of America's best beaches — for a final morning swim in crystal-clear waters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the historic Parker Ranch in Waimea for a taste of Hawaiian paniolo (cowboy) culture, or explore the premium boutiques and galleries of Waimea town. Stop at a local macadamia nut farm for a tasting tour. Begin packing and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at the resort's signature restaurant celebrating an unforgettable 10-day Hawaii adventure. Arrange private luxury transfer to Kona International Airport (KOA) for the return flight to the mainland.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely final resort breakfast — fresh Hawaiian fruit platters, eggs Benedict with kalua pork, and Kona coffee grown on the slopes of Hualalai volcano
meals.lunch: Merriman's Market Café in Waimea — the original farm-to-table Hawaii restaurant by chef Peter Merriman, featuring locally grown produce and Big Island beef
meals.dinner: Beach Tree Restaurant at Four Seasons Hualalai — elegant open-air beachfront dining with wood-fired cuisine, fresh seafood, and tropical cocktails for a perfect farewell

day_by_day.notes: Manta ray night snorkel tours depart from Keauhou Bay and are a bucket-list Big Island experience — book in advance through the hotel concierge. Confirm return flight details and arrange airport transfer at least 3 hours before departure. Kona Airport (KOA) is a small open-air airport — arrive 2 hours early for domestic flights. Purchase final Hawaiian souvenirs at the resort gift shop or Waimea boutiques. Mahalo for an incredible Hawaii adventure!
